## Notes

- The PR satisfies the selected documentation rubrics: the rename from “deployment” to “setup” makes the entry point more reader-task-oriented, while workflow/action docs move into a usage section that better matches user intent.
- I fetched live PR metadata and diff with `gh`; the PR has no comments, reviews, labels, or parent/tracking issue references in the body.

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: 8e40e3f777cb18e0c3b55484db5850c567132d5d -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #335 reorganizes Sepo documentation sections so first-time setup, normal usage, architecture, and technical details are separated more clearly.
- It renames `deployment/` docs to `setup/`, moves workflow/action docs into `usage/`, and moves the orchestrator doc into architecture.
- The PR also updates links in docs, skills, source constants, and path-sensitive tests.
- The current PR body and discussion do not reference a parent or tracking issue.

## Review
The reorganization is sound and most reviewers agree the link/path sweep is complete. The remaining required work is minor terminology cleanup, with one optional label-alignment note for the flat docs index.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Stale deployment terminology remains | WARNING | After renaming the docs section to setup, two visible references still say “deployment” in contexts that point readers at the renamed setup docs. |
| Flat index still says Actions for Using Sepo | INFO | `.agent/docs/index.md` now links into `usage/`, but the visible flat-list label still says `Actions overview` under `Actions:` instead of matching `Using Sepo`. |

## Progress
- Rubrics review passed: the PR stays surgical, updates path-sensitive tests, and follows the docs navigation pattern.
- Codex review reported `npm --prefix .agent test` passed with 672 tests.
- Existing inline comments and review threads were empty before synthesis.
- Posted one inline comment on `.agent/docs/index.md:110` for the `Actions overview` / `Using Sepo` label mismatch.
- No inline comments were replied to, minimized, or resolved.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Stale deployment terminology remains</summary>

**Cause:** The rename updated paths and section metadata, but unchanged prose still says `deployment` in [`self-hosted-github-action-runner.md#L18`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/8e40e3f777cb18e0c3b55484db5850c567132d5d/.agent/docs/setup/self-hosted-github-action-runner.md#L18) and [`README.md#L106`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/8e40e3f777cb18e0c3b55484db5850c567132d5d/README.md#L106).

**Candidate solutions:** Change “this deployment page” to “this setup page” and “deployment options” to “setup options” or another setup-oriented phrase.

**Comments:** This is not blocking, but it is directly tied to the PR’s stated rename from deployment docs to setup docs.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Flat index still says Actions for Using Sepo</summary>

**Cause:** The docs index now points `Actions overview` at `usage/index.md`, while the destination page and sidebar label are `Using Sepo`.

**Candidate solutions:** Rename the flat-list header from `Actions:` to `Using Sepo:` and/or rename `Actions overview` to `Using Sepo overview`.

**Comments:** This is cosmetic and was posted inline at `.agent/docs/index.md:110`: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/335#discussion_r3280664616

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
`FIX_PR`: the stale setup/deployment wording is a concrete, safe docs cleanup for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
`MINOR_ISSUES`

## Action Items
- [ ] Update the remaining setup-related prose that still says “deployment” in the self-hosted runner doc and README.

## Rubrics Update

No changes were committed to [`agent/rubrics`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/tree/agent/rubrics) from PR #335.

no rubric changes

PR #335 had no trusted maintainer/user feedback that introduced a new durable preference. The only discussion and review comments were bot-authored, and the trusted PR body described the specific docs reorganization rather than a reusable rubric. Existing rubrics already cover the relevant themes: audience-first docs, actionable setup guidance, keeping docs in sync, and surgical changes. Rubrics checkout remains clean.
